title: microsaas-llm-pricing-play-notes
content:
Purpose: rough personal notebook for a micro‑SaaS pricing experiment using Redwood hosted API. Aim is to sketch per-customer economics for a tiny vertical app that uses streaming chat and embeddings. Not for circulation yet — very raw.

Topline assumptions (example app):
- Active customers: 500 target in yr1 (monthly paying)
- Average MAU per customer: 2 users (paid seats)
- Sessions per user per month: 25 (short micro-interactions, median 45s)
- Average tokens per session: 600 (prompt + response; streaming enabled)
- Embedding calls: 2 per session (small index lookups), avg 768-d embedding at 1 request = 0.5k tokens equivalent for cost model

Goal metrics to estimate: ARPU, gross margin per customer, payback period on acquisition (CAC), and sensible price tiers.

Base token cost assumptions (hosted):
- Model: rdx-small (hypothetical) => $0.0009 per 1k tokens input+output combined (we'll treat as blended)
- Embedding cost: $0.001 per embedding (per 768-d)
- Infra + overhead amortized: add 20% on top of token/embedding costs for routing, logging, retries

Per-customer monthly usage (calc):
- tokens: 2 users * 25 sessions * 600 tokens = 30,000 tokens / month
- token cost: 30k tokens * ($0.0009 / 1000) = $0.027 per customer / month (base)
- embeddings: 25 sessions * 2 = 50 embeddings -> 50 * $0.001 = $0.05 per customer / month
- subtotal per customer (direct API costs): $0.077
- + 20% infra overhead => $0.0924 (round to $0.09)

This looks tiny because token rate assumed is quite low — check: maybe blended should be $0.006 / 1k for higher-quality model. Recalc:
- if token price = $0.006 / 1k -> token cost = 30k * 0.006 / 1000 = $0.18
- embeddings same $0.05 -> subtotal $0.23 -> +20% = $0.276 ~= $0.28 per customer/month

So range: $0.09–$0.28 cost/customer/month. Add customer support, infra, amortized feature development, and payment fees. Quick rule: target gross margin >= 70% for self-serve; aim price >= 3x variable cost.

Tier sketch (rounded):
- Free: up to 10 sessions / month, limited embeddings, no SLA
- Starter: $4 / month -> aimed at hobby / viral growth (covers costs if cost/customer~$0.3 -> gross margin ~92%)
- Pro: $15 / month -> teams, more sessions (x5), priority queues
- Team: $75 / month -> seat-based, includes higher concurrency, increased retention window

Back-of-envelope ARPU & revenue: assume conversion from free to paid 4% of signups; ARR at 500 customers (split 60% Starter, 30% Pro, 10% Team):
- Starter (300) * $4 = $1,200 / month
- Pro (150) * $15 = $2,250 / month
- Team (50) * $75 = $3,750 / month
- Total = $7,200 / month -> $86.4k ARR (not great, but microsaas scale)

Customer economics: with average variable cost (using conservative $0.28) -> weighted avg cost per customer:
- Starter: assume usage at baseline (1x) => cost $0.28
- Pro: 5x usage -> cost $1.4
- Team: 20x usage -> cost $5.6
- Weighted avg (300*0.28 + 150*1.4 + 50*5.6)/500 = (84 + 210 + 280)/500 = 574/500 = $1.148 per customer / month.
- Gross margin = (ARPU average ~ $7.2k/500 = $14.4/month) -> (14.4 - 1.15)/14.4 = 92% roughly. (Starter heavy mix keeps margin high)

Sensitivity notes:
- If we onboard higher-quality model for core generation (e.g., rdx-medium @ $0.02 / 1k), cost balloons. Need caching/prefix reuse to avoid per-request cost.
- Conversational caching: 40% of tokens are repetition/short prompts -> can be cached/prefetched (saves ~0.4x tokens) if we can guarantee typical UX.
- Batching and KV cache on dedicated pool reduces effective token unit cost by ~20% for high concurrency tenants. Consider offering Pro-tier with "runtime-optimized" option as value-add.

Pricing experiments to try (quick A/B):
1) Credit pack model: $5 for 10k tokens non-expiring (helps power-users). Monitor token redemption and ARPU uplift.
2) Session bundles: 50 sessions / month $12 vs per-seat $15 (test absolute vs seat-based).
3) Latency SLA add-on: +$20/mo for 99.9% edge routing and priority fallback to dedicated pool (appeals to enterprise trials).

Pilot metrics to track (instrumentation):
- tokens per session distribution (p50/p90/p99)
- embeddings per session and percentage of sessions that call embed
- prefix cache hit rate and avg token savings per session
- churn by usage bucket (0-5, 6-25, 25+)
- conversion funnel free -> paid and ARPU by cohort

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Validate embedding cost: vendor rates vary (some models charge per 1k tokens for embeddings) -> need canonical rates table.
- How to price when we assume customers will use higher-quality generations intentionally (answer: offer quality toggle + clear pricing multiplier).
- Decide whether to round prices to psychological anchors ($4, $15) vs cost-based fractional pricing.
- Legal: do we need to disallow vector uploads that greatly increase async compute costs for free tier? (ping legal + infra)

Quick notes on acquisition payback: 
- If CAC = $30 (paid acquisition), and average revenue per customer = $14.4/mo, payback < 3 months if gross margin healthy. But CAC needs to be validated.

Implementation / product hooks:
- Expose per-route/feature metering in console so customers can see token vs embedding spend (helps justify higher tiers).
- Add "session saver" control that compresses context for older messages to reduce token burn (value prop for Pro).
- Consider offering credits for early adopters (e.g., 3 months free for first 100 customers) and model impact on ARR.

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally terse. Next steps: run a simulator notebook with realistic token-size distribution (p50 350, p90 1.8k) and recalc costs with alternate model price tiers. Link results into GH PR above and add experiment flags for credit packs.

End.
